records.description: For the Penedo noncleavable I-III FRET construct, the loop-carrying form shows a magnesium-dependent decrease in FRET described by a two-state concentration fit with midpoint 160 micromolar and Hill coefficient 0.85. Sodium produces two resolved titration transitions even in the loop-carrying form; adding moderate sodium to a 100 micromolar magnesium background first reverses and then restores the FRET shift.

records.name: Preparation-dependent membrane morphology
openObligations: Read the complete actual primary main article pages 153-165 and complete PMC HTML, all seven figures, all three tables, Methods/References, plus the complete six-page publisher Supporting Information with all four figures and procedures. The university PDF adds a repository cover. Primary supplement identity is verified by ACS figshare DOI 10.1021/acssynbio.7b00265.s001 and file 9445870; original PMC files were unread HTML challenges.

This reconstitution supplies purified mature enzymes and pre-existing phospholipid liposomes; enzymes and substrates are added externally. The source explicitly says this pathway does not support de novo membrane synthesis because PlsB and other components require existing phospholipids/membranes. No first membrane, protein biosynthesis origin, self-reproducing cell or self-made enzyme complement is established.

The selected chemistry context is the three-enzyme PA time course in SI Figure S3. It is distinct from the full eight-enzyme headgroup pathway and the PE/PG endpoint/calibration assays. SI specifies different PlsB/ATP concentrations for that time course than the general main PA procedure; these are retained as different preparations, not silently pooled.

LC-MS records internal-standard-normalized ion counts and source-assigned lipid identities. Species-dependent response, extraction recovery, peak integration and external calibration govern concentration/yield inference. The main text refers to PE/PG standards in Supporting Information, but the retrieved six-page supplement contains no explicit PE/PG calibration curve; no independent absolute-yield or uncertainty reconstruction is made.

Limiting-CoA conversion supports source-specific cofactor recycling, with supplied ATP and substrates. It does not close energy/resource supply, synthesize fatty-acid chains from carbon feedstock, make every phospholipid or show indefinite throughput. Small PA signal without PlsC is source-attributed to possible PlsC contamination of PlsB; omission effects are not treated as perfectly pure single-enzyme controls.

R18 self-quenching is a membrane dye-dilution proxy. In Figure 6 the immediate fluorescence increase follows oleic-acid addition and does not require phospholipid biosynthesis; subsequent PA conversion adds little further fluorescence change. Thus the signal alone cannot isolate synthesis-driven area growth from fatty-acid partition, swelling, fusion or dye redistribution.

The source reports an approximate 25-30 percent expansion from R18 assumptions. No new exact area/volume expansion, vesicle number, leaflet distribution, size distribution or calibrated membrane material balance is independently admitted. Triton-normalized maximal emission is not a direct bilayer surface-area standard.

R18 PA conversion uses 2.7 mM oleic acid and three enzymes. Figure 7 morphology follows a different PG-pathway preparation and a 1.5 mM total fatty-acid feed. These are not matched single-vesicle samples or an interchangeable protocol. Cryo-EM snapshots are not longitudinal lineage/continuous growth tracking.

High-dose material forms stacked multilamellar-like structures that resolve after EDTA. The dosed-feed comparison also lowers magnesium; exact lower magnesium concentration is not resolved in the reviewed main/SI descriptions. Feeding and magnesium are changed together, so an isolated feeding or magnesium causal effect is not established.

The PA-divalent-cation/outer-leaflet imbalance/slow-flip-flop explanation is a source hypothesis. No direct leaflet-resolved synthesis, flip-flop kinetics, cation binding map, complete membrane retention, permeability/selectivity panel, electrochemical gradient or transport activity is measured here.

The title continuous refers to CoA reuse and finite precursor conversion; the conclusion proposes a future continuously controlled feeding system. Finite time courses/endpoints and supplied doses do not demonstrate indefinite membrane production, balanced division, autonomous enzyme renewal or population self-reproduction.
No universal efficiency/robustness benefit, compartmentalized competing metabolism, spontaneous origin sequence, adaptive regulation or required prior metabolic compartment is established.

records.description: Engineer N-end-rule-tagged E. coli DHFR/cpLys38, selected C-terminally tagged cpLys38, lysine-less unstructured-tail additions, terminal His6 and linear Ub4 variants as defined in Figures 2-5. cpLys38 joins the old termini with six glycines and starts at former Lys38/ends at Asn37. Prewarm25 C for 3 min; initiate with 0.5 mM ATP,10 mM creatine phosphate and 0.1mg/ml creatine phosphokinase. Compare320 micromolar methotrexate with equal-DMSO controls where indicated. Quench time points into SDS-PAGE buffer and quantify radiolabeled full-length/ubiquitinated bands, fragments and, for the separate purified His6 substrate, terminal-epitope immunoblots.

limitations: These are engineered E. coli DHFR/cpLys38/barnase substrate constructs in rabbit reticulocyte lysate, not a universal survey of naturally damaged proteins or an intact-cell misfolding-surveillance experiment.

Proteasome attribution follows the source lysate assay. No separately purified proteasome, newly isolated E1/E2/E3 requirement, new receptor-binding measurement, ATPase-step assay, translocation movie, force measurement or proteasome-inhibitor control is supplied by the selected main panels.

SDS-PAGE/autoradiography quantifies remaining full-length plus ubiquitinated forms as defined by each panel; His6 immunoblotting localizes loss of a terminal epitope. Band loss, tail clipping, complete destruction and production/reuse of free amino acids are different outcomes.

The source tests folded and methotrexate-stabilized proteins. The assays do not establish that only misfolded proteins are degraded, that native proteins are excluded, or that the proteasome itself decides whether a client is damaged.

The engineered linear Ub4 tag has four N-to-C fused ubiquitin moieties with G76V substitutions. It is not a newly measured native Lys48-isopeptide-linked polyubiquitin chain or an independently observed covalent ubiquitination reaction.

No universal requirement for ubiquitination is admitted; the paper itself cites ubiquitin-independent cases as background. Recognition, initiation, unfolding and proteolysis remain distinct, with the detailed unfolding/pulling cycle conditional.

No raw autoradiograms, numerical rate fit, binding constant, precise substrate concentration or kinetic uncertainty is reconstructed. Exact engineered tail amino-acid sequences are not printed in the reviewed main Methods, and no universal20-residue minimum is admitted from data-not-shown observations.

The ubiquitination control adds2 micromolar Ubal to inhibit deubiquitination and 320 micromolar methotrexate to inhibit degradation. Its accumulating ubiquitin-band signal is a net assay readout under those conditions, not direct matched receptor occupancy or one isolated E1/E2/E3 rate.

Similar source ubiquitination kinetics for full versus shortened N-end-rule tags constrain reduced tagging as the explanation for the deletion effect. They do not prove equal proteasome-binding occupancy or exact chain topology.
Selected degradation panels use 25 C and 0.5 mM ATP with regeneration; Figure 1 two-domain direction assays use 30 C and are not silently treated as the same condition.

C-terminal tail effects differ between cpLys38 and wild-type DHFR under 320 micromolar methotrexate: the former can be degraded whereas the latter can be clipped while the stabilized DHFR remains. A tag or tail does not guarantee complete degradation of every substrate.

Tail disorder is a source assignment supported by the paper separate4 C nonspecific-protease sensitivity assay and a hydrodynamic statement partly data-not-shown. It is not a newly solved structure or an independent measurement of every tail conformation.

The global-unfolding control is a GroEL-binding/protease-protection assay at 15 C with 100 micromolar methotrexate. Degradation uses 25 C and 320 micromolar methotrexate; a similar control trace is not proof of identical local stability or kinetics under every degradation condition.

Nonspecific protease sensitivity and GroEL capture are operational readouts. A similar source global-unfolding trace does not exclude local changes or establish an exact thermodynamic free-energy identity.
